method: Human review of extracted theorem statements, retained definitions and section/typeclass context; proof bodies followed for load-bearing links as recorded. Existing kernel receipt is separate evidence. A reviewed statement does not mean its full physical application has been constructed.

Greatestness.assessment: LexLt is first strict coordinate with all earlier coordinates equal. Aligned means membership plus no strict feasible improvement. The no-needless-loss equivalence follows these definitions. The union-closure theorem upgrades maximality to componentwise greatestness by forming o sup q. strict_except_mirrors and aligned_unique retain that closure input.
application_obligations: Construct the intended outcome coordinates and actual feasible family; closure is needed on the resource branch where this theorem is used.
private_helpers: exists_first_diff uses finite n, not a choice over an unrestricted infinite lexicographic order.

Law.role: Finite existence, standby life guard, full-scope criterion, faithful-hold comparison
Law.assessment: Finite nonempty F supplies an aligned option; life_guard retains stage-zero standby outcomes with n>0. scope_guarantee_iff quantifies over every feasible family of subsets and correctly forces full scope within the chosen index type. Faithful-hold dominance transfers supplied statewise canonical dominance to upward events. Strictness needs finite measure, measurability and positive missed mass.
application_obligations: Bind the index type to the entire intended physical domain.
Construct the statewise faithful hold; the measure theorem does not construct it.

UnionClosure.role: Resource feasibility, greatestness, solvent and finite-slack alternatives
UnionClosure.assessment: budgetFamily explicitly intersects realisability with the cost bound. Affordable dominance uses a realisable join and its affordability; finite-slack dominance also uses subadditive cost. aligned_eq_of_greatest is an order result using a supplied greatest feasible tuple. greatest_of_solvent takes htopR and hsolv independently. greatest_or_irrelevant retains htopR at every step and a cost/demand correspondence. Its negative branch is a first negative ledger balance. insolvent_not_greatest is a finite counterexample and does not refute the solvent theorem.
application_obligations: G2: construct the full realisable top tuple.
Supply the actual cost and funding correspondence; the negative branch does not itself supply protection.

SolventReciprocity.assessment: solvent_keeps_everyone substitutes o=top from UnionClosure and applies htopkeeps. The rival premise in reciprocity_dominance_solvent is deliberately unnecessary because everyone is already kept. No union closure or rival feasibility premise remains on this branch.
application_obligations: htopkeeps supplies the physical continuation interpretation.
G2 supplies realisability; solvency supplies affordability.
SolventReciprocity.settled_result: Do not reopen the request for a solvent reciprocity restatement; both statements are already present.

AffordableReciprocity.assessment: Derives the keeps consequence from UnionClosure.dominates_of_affordable and monotonicity of keeps. It retains UnionRealizable, rival realisability and affordability of the join; it does not require family-wide budget closure.
application_obligations: Use on the stated resource branch with the actual join certificate.
AffordableReciprocity.settled_result: Present in the canon; register text describing it as still held/banked is stale.

PremiseFloor.role: Ledger dichotomy, deficit forcing, first-stage comparison and reversible-administration argument
PremiseFloor.assessment: balance is initial escrow plus the finite sum of income minus demand. income_or_irrelevance is a classical nonnegative-or-first-negative dichotomy. forced_breach needs cumulative net deficit tending to infinity. breach_strictly_below receives strict first-stage loss. reversible_administration_forced receives a feasible counterpart preserving earlier stages and strictly improving the resource stage.
application_obligations: Bind demand to the complete physical cost.
The reversible counterpart is constructed in the Bennett route, not by this order lemma alone.
Necessary funding and actual availability of that funding are distinct.

ReciprocityCeiling.role: Union-closed reciprocity and geometric finite-account ceiling
ReciprocityCeiling.assessment: The original reciprocity theorem retains hF, correctly superseded on the solvent branch by SolventReciprocity. ceiling_achievable assumes uniform geometric account bounds A_i r^d with 0<=r<1 and a finite account set, then obtains every positive ceiling at sufficiently large distance.
application_obligations: Supply the actual below-threshold account law; the convergence lemma does not establish the physical noise model.
ReciprocityCeiling.settled_result: No new union-closure demand on the solvent branch.

ReasonsRoute.assessment: Option-value results compare a maximum with the immediate destructive payoff under nonnegative normalised rational weights; strictness needs a positive-weight strict improvement. Regime.law is defined with protects=True. law_protects_everyone and indicator_law therefore establish the representation's definitions. Finite rival fractions are bounded by one and strictly below one if a member fails to keep m.
application_obligations: The physical all-preserving regime comes from G1/G2, not from protects=True.
A general ensemble of objectives needs its own interpretation; the source proves finite indicator statements.
ReasonsRoute.settled_result: The accepted reasons-or-holding route remains; this does not introduce universal voluntary adoption as a requirement.

ReasonsCompiled.role: Good-event expectation comparisons and controller recovery floor
ReasonsCompiled.assessment: reciprocity_expectation concludes rival-event mass <= canonical-event mass + mass(G complement), given dominance on G. canonical_floor uses a measurable good event and top on G. Strictness needs rival missed mass larger than mass(G complement). reciprocity_from_solvency obtains top on G from realisability, affordability and alignment. controller_pays_floor is the RecoveryWork admitted-protocol inequality, and controller_floor_diverges is the associated real-power asymptotic.
application_obligations: Trace the current Section 15.2 unconditional probability display to an all-world dominance or common-failure coupling support; the additive charged-event allowance cannot simply be erased.
ReasonsCompiled.trace_status: Support tracing pending through BridgeD1, Law and accepted common-history arguments; not classified as a new theory gap.

Irreplaceability.assessment: value is a sum of assigned real information weights. Erasing a member loses exactly its assigned weight; positive weight gives strict loss. An optimum under a cardinality budget cannot omit a higher-weight available item while retaining a lower-weight one.
application_obligations: Use the stated additive model. Bind weights to genuinely irreplaceable information where the physical interpretation is made; arbitrary joint mutual information is not automatically additive.
